name: バンコックコスモ食堂 (Bangkok Cosmo Shokudo)

claims.text: The kitchen is particular about ingredient sourcing — it uses genuine holy basil from Thai-run contract farms for its gapao dishes rather than a substitute, suggesting attentiveness to authentic, unadulterated flavors.

The signature tonkatsu is coated in fresh wheat panko and fried in a shared corn-salad-oil and sesame-oil blend used across the fried menu; no gluten-free fryer or breading alternative was identified in any source.

name: カフェ アンド マクロビ (Cafe and MACROBI)

claims.text: Vegetable-forward daily lunch plates using produce sourced from Aoyama Farmers Market growers, prepared under a macrobiotic cooking instructor's supervision.

name: セイロンドロップ (Ceylon Drop)

claims.text: The standard curry set (Sri Lanka Plate) pairs a chicken curry with a separate vegetable curry on the same plate, giving those avoiding meat a plant-based curry option without a special request.

name: 茶庭 然花抄院 渋谷ヒカリエ ShinQs店 (Chatei Zen Kashoin Shibuya Hikarie ShinQs)

claims.text: Signature castella and most confections are made with wheat flour in the same shop kitchen used for all items; no dedicated gluten-free prep area or allergy protocol was found.
Castella is made with egg yolks and milk; parfait and kakigori menu items include dairy toppings. No vegan-specific menu, ingredient substitution, or preparation process was found.

name: 中華麺店 喜楽 (Chuka Menten Kiraku)

claims.text: The signature broth is soy-sauce (shoyu) based, which in Japan is almost always wheat-containing; no wheat-free tamari or gluten-free soy sauce option was found in any source.
The dojō are cooked in sake and soy sauce and then simmered in a shallow iron pot with the house's soy-sauce-based warishita sauce, a recipe unchanged and passed down since the restaurant's founding.

The restaurant is a French bistro built around meat- and fish-based courses with a vegetable-forward philosophy layered on top, not a vegetarian or vegan kitchen — classic French technique (butter, cream, meat/fish stock) should be assumed in dishes not specifically flagged as plant-based.
The kitchen's stated concept centers on sourcing fresh, seasonal vegetables directly through relationships with trusted producers, and building courses around them.
